Activity: Decide whether a new feature or design change affects security, and bring in product security
Note: The product owner owns the decision to engage; engineers usually spot the change first. Many organizations make this a checklist item at design reviews.

Activity: Plan security activities and deliverables into the project schedule
Note: Security work that isn't on the schedule gets squeezed out. Program management owns the plan; product security says what's needed.

Activity: Threat model the product and assess security risk
Note: Product security usually leads, but engineers who know the design do much of the work. Clinical input on harm matters. Some organizations make engineering accountable, with product security reviewing.

Activity: Define security requirements and trace them to tests
Note: Requirements belong to the product, so they follow the normal requirements process; product security advises on content.

Activity: Select third-party and open-source components and keep the SBOM current
Note: Engineering chooses components and maintains the SBOM; product security reviews risk; supply chain covers commercial suppliers.

Activity: Run security testing, including penetration testing
Note: Often product security or an independent tester performs penetration testing; engineering runs security requirements tests.

Activity: Prepare the cybersecurity content of the regulatory submission
Note: Regulatory owns the submission; product security writes or assembles most of the security content.
Most organizations have a PSIRT within or alongside product security. Service and sales need to know where to send anything they hear.

Activity: Assess a vulnerability's patient-safety impact (controlled or uncontrolled risk)
Note: The safety risk owner, often in quality, is accountable for the risk file; product security brings the exploitability view.

Activity: Communicate with customers about a vulnerability and its mitigations
Note: This varies widely. Some organizations make product security or a communications team accountable. Everyone customer-facing should use the same approved message.

Activity: Answer hospital security questionnaires and provide the MDS2 form
Note: Sales usually runs the process with the customer; product security owns the accuracy of the answers.

Activity: Decide and announce a product's end of support
Note: End of support is a business decision with security and regulatory consequences. Customers need it well in advance.

Activity: Include security requirements in supplier contracts
Note: Supply chain owns contracts; product security defines what suppliers must do, such as notifying you about vulnerabilities in their components.
